decisions.reason: It fits closely with the firm's established precast automation and integrated plant know-how, and the firm's strong in-house R&D makes it likely to learn from early market experience and improve rather than withdraw it.

As an automation module that builds directly on the firm's existing shuttering, controls, and plant-engineering capabilities, it is well within the firm's absorptive capacity and therefore likely to be retained.

Although somewhat more niche than the core shuttering robots, it still builds on the firm's existing production-line and handling expertise, so a technologically capable German machinery firm with its own R&D would usually keep developing it.

Automatic shuttering is central to the firm's established offer and strategic direction toward future-ready automated precast production, which makes continued market presence more likely than withdrawal.
